prompt.brief: Design a global Instagram-like photo and video sharing platform for uploads, profiles, follows, personalized feeds, stories, likes, comments, and discovery.
successSignals: Keep media bytes, metadata, social graph state, and feed projections in independently scalable systems.
Use direct resumable uploads, asynchronous media processing, object storage, and a CDN for large assets.
Choose a hybrid feed strategy that protects the system from celebrity fanout explosions.
Explain privacy, moderation, deletion, story expiry, retries, and eventual consistency explicitly.

functional: Users upload photos and videos, edit captions, publish posts, and view profile timelines.
Users follow or unfollow accounts and receive a personalized home feed.
Users publish stories that expire after 24 hours and can like, comment on, or share content.
Users search accounts and hashtags while enforcing private-account, block, moderation, and deletion rules.
nonFunctional: Media upload acknowledgement should not wait for transcoding or thumbnail generation.
Target p95 below 200 ms for a cached feed page and below 2 seconds for ordinary media readiness.
Feed reads should remain bounded even when a followed account has millions of followers.
Retries, duplicate events, worker loss, cache loss, and regional degradation must be recoverable.
scaleAssumptions: 500 million daily active users, 100 million media uploads per day, and 10 million peak concurrent viewers.
Most accounts have fewer than 1,000 followees, but a small creator set has tens of millions of followers.
Each upload creates multiple image or video renditions and thumbnails stored with lifecycle policies.
Stories have a 24-hour visibility window, while takedowns and privacy changes take effect immediately.

metrics.label: Media upload rate
metrics.description: 100M uploads per day before burst and retry headroom.

metrics.label: Feed read latency
metrics.description: Serve a cursor page from a bounded projection and cache.

metrics.label: Media readiness
metrics.description: Required renditions become playable asynchronously after upload.

metrics.label: Story lifetime
metrics.description: Expiry is enforced in reads and by cleanup workers.

entities.name: MediaAsset
entities.notes: Store bytes in object storage and keep lifecycle and processing metadata in a database.

entities.name: Post
entities.notes: The durable source record is separate from feed entries and counters.

entities.name: Story
entities.notes: Expiry is a serving constraint, not a reason to rely only on a cache TTL.

entities.name: FollowEdge
entities.notes: Maintain both follower and following access paths for fanout and profile queries.

entities.name: FeedEntry
entities.notes: A rebuildable projection; celebrity posts can be merged during reads.

entities.name: Interaction
entities.notes: At-least-once consumers deduplicate by event or actor-object key.

apis.contract: { contentType, size, checksum, requestId } -> { uploadId, partUrls }
apis.notes: Authorize first and issue signed multipart URLs so large bytes bypass the API tier.

apis.contract: { uploadId, caption, visibility, requestId } -> { postId, state }
apis.notes: Commit metadata idempotently after object storage confirms the upload.
Read a bounded projection, merge hot-author candidates, and recheck policy.
Return only visible, unexpired stories and short-cache the manifest.
Use an actor-post uniqueness key and publish an idempotent interaction event.
Update graph state once and emit a relationship event for feed maintenance.

dataFlow.title: Reserve a resumable upload
dataFlow.description: The client requests signed part URLs, uploads directly to object storage, and retries individual parts by checksum.

dataFlow.title: Commit the content record
dataFlow.description: The API validates ownership and policy, writes post or story metadata, and returns a durable identifier.

dataFlow.title: Process media asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Workers scan, resize, transcode, and write rendition manifests; failed jobs retry through a dead-letter queue.

dataFlow.title: Build the feed projection
dataFlow.description: Publication events fan out to ordinary followers, while high-follower authors are merged on read or through a hybrid shard.

dataFlow.title: Serve and invalidate asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Feed and story reads use cursors, cache, and CDN URLs while counters, notifications, analytics, expiry, and deletion consumers catch up independently.

architecture.title: Instagram-style media and feed architecture
architecture.summary: Clients upload directly to object storage; durable content and graph services publish events to processing, feed, interaction, notification, and moderation consumers.

layers.label: Global Instagram-like photo request boundary
layers.description: Clients and edge services handle uploads, reads, authentication, and media delivery.

layers.label: Durable source state
layers.description: Content metadata, ownership, visibility, and social graph records.

layers.label: Asynchronous projections
layers.description: Media processing, event transport, feed fanout, and rebuildable read models.

layers.label: Extensions
layers.description: Interactions, moderation, notifications, analytics, and operational monitoring.

keyPaths.label: Publish path
keyPaths.description: Client -> signed object upload -> content service -> durable record -> processing events.

keyPaths.label: Feed read path
keyPaths.description: Client -> feed service -> projection and hot-author merge -> signed CDN media URLs.

keyPaths.label: Hybrid fanout path
keyPaths.description: Publication event -> fanout policy -> follower projection or pull-on-read candidates.

components.description: Upload media, browse feeds and stories, and submit social actions.

components.description: Authenticates requests, applies quotas, and issues signed upload URLs.

components.label: Object storage

components.label: Content service
components.description: Owns posts, stories, visibility, expiry, deletion, and publication state.

components.label: Content database
components.description: Stores durable metadata and moderation state keyed by content and owner.

components.label: Social graph service
components.description: Manages follows, blocks, private-account policy, and relationship reads.

components.label: Graph store
components.description: Stores adjacency lists and relationship versions for efficient fanout checks.

components.label: Media workers
components.description: Scan, resize, transcode, and publish rendition manifests asynchronously.

components.label: Global Instagram-like photo event backbone
components.description: Retains publication, graph, interaction, deletion, and moderation events for replay.

components.label: Hybrid fanout service
components.description: Pushes normal authors and uses pull or hybrid delivery for celebrity authors.

components.label: Feed projection store
components.description: Stores bounded cursor-friendly feed entries and story indexes.

components.label: Feed and story service
components.description: Reads projections, merges hot-author candidates, and applies visibility and expiry filters.

components.label: Media CDN
components.description: Serves signed rendition URLs near viewers and supports purge on takedown.

components.label: Interaction service
components.description: Commits likes and comments with actor-object uniqueness and event publication.

components.label: Moderation service
components.description: Scans media and reports, then emits takedown or appeal decisions.

components.label: Notifications
components.description: Delivers selected follows and interactions with preferences and retries.

components.label: Analytics and discovery
components.description: Consumes events for ranking features, search, recommendations, and abuse signals.

components.label: Global Instagram-like photo monitoring
components.description: Tracks upload readiness, feed lag, fanout backlog, CDN hit rate, and expiry correctness.

connections.label: API requests
connections.description: Authenticated content, graph, feed, and interaction commands.

connections.label: Direct upload
connections.description: Large media bytes use signed URLs and bypass application servers.

connections.label: Publish metadata
connections.description: Content service validates and commits the source record.

connections.label: Durable state
connections.description: Posts, stories, ownership, visibility, and processing state.

connections.label: Content events
connections.description: Publication and lifecycle events are replayable.

connections.label: Fanout
connections.description: Publication drives the selected push or pull strategy.

connections.label: Feed entries
connections.description: Projection writes are sharded by viewer.

connections.label: Read feed
connections.description: Feed requests carry cursor and policy context.

connections.label: Projection read
connections.description: Cursor pages are read without scanning all follows.

connections.label: Media URLs
connections.description: The service returns signed rendition URLs.

connections.label: Interaction stream
connections.description: Counters, notifications, and analytics consume the same durable events.

connections.label: Policy checks
connections.description: Moderation can quarantine and invalidate content asynchronously.

connections.label: Product events
connections.description: Discovery and abuse pipelines are decoupled from reads.

deepDives.title: Hybrid feed fanout
points: Push ordinary-author posts into a bounded per-user inbox for fast reads.
Pull celebrity posts at read time or write them to a small set of shards.
Use a versioned cursor and deduplicate post IDs after merging candidates.

deepDives.title: Media processing and delivery
points: Use checksum-based multipart retries and immutable object keys.
Generate a bounded rendition set and publish a manifest only after required outputs are ready.
Use signed CDN URLs, short metadata caches, and purge events for deletion or moderation.

deepDives.title: Privacy, deletion, and expiry
points: Recheck follow, block, private-account, moderation, and expiry state at read time.
Tombstone source records before asynchronous projection and CDN cleanup.
Run expiry sweeps as repair work even when story TTL notifications are delayed.

deepDives.title: Exactly-once user experience
points: Make post, follow, like, and comment commands idempotent with request IDs.
Deduplicate at consumers because the stream is at-least-once.
Return optimistic UI state with a server version so reconnects can reconcile safely.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull feeds
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use hybrid fanout: push normal accounts and pull high-follower accounts.
tradeoffs.caution: The threshold and merge logic add complexity and require lag monitoring.

tradeoffs.title: Strong versus eventual counters
tradeoffs.recommendation: Make the actor-object relationship authoritative and derive displayed counts asynchronously.
tradeoffs.caution: Counts can briefly lag; expose reconciliation rather than blocking the interaction.

tradeoffs.title: One store versus specialized stores
tradeoffs.recommendation: Separate object storage, graph access, source metadata, and projections by access pattern.
tradeoffs.caution: Cross-store workflows need events, repair jobs, and clear ownership boundaries.

tradeoffs.title: Synchronous versus asynchronous moderation
tradeoffs.recommendation: Run cheap safety checks before publication and deeper scanning asynchronously.
tradeoffs.caution: Every serving path must honor a later quarantine or deletion decision.

commonMistakes: Proxying every media byte through the API servers.
Faning out a celebrity post synchronously to every follower.
Treating feed entries or CDN caches as the source of truth.
Relying only on cache TTLs for story expiry and deletion.
Assuming event delivery is exactly once or ignoring consumer deduplication.
Checking privacy only when writing a feed entry instead of rechecking on reads.

followUps.question: How do you handle a creator with 50 million followers?
followUps.answer: Keep the creator out of synchronous per-follower fanout, partition pull candidates, and merge them into bounded feed reads with a short cache.

followUps.question: What happens when media processing is delayed?
followUps.answer: Return an upload or post state that is durable but not ready, retry workers from the queue, and expose readiness without blocking feed metadata.

followUps.question: How do unfollows and blocks affect already-built feeds?
followUps.answer: Emit graph events to remove entries, but also apply relationship and visibility checks while serving so stale projections cannot leak content.

followUps.question: How would you rebuild a lost feed projection?
followUps.answer: Replay publication and graph events from retention, backfill recent source posts, and atomically advance a per-user projection version.

rubric.description: Direct upload, durable metadata, asynchronous rendition generation, and CDN delivery are clearly separated.
The answer explains hybrid fanout, celebrity handling, cursor reads, and rebuildable projections.
Idempotency, at-least-once events, visibility checks, deletion, moderation, and expiry are addressed.
The design includes lag metrics, retries, replay, repair jobs, regional degradation, and capacity assumptions.
